security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around skill names, prompt examples, and a diagram in SKILL.md. No executable scripts, shell invocation, network access, credential access, or prompt injection text were found in the reviewed file.

remediation.issue: Markdown backticks trigger external command heuristics.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the content as documentation, or replace unnecessary inline code formatting with plain text where marketplace scanners do not need it.

remediation.issue: Workflow depends on other named skills.
remediation.suggestion: List required companion skills clearly so users understand this bundle is an orchestration guide and not a standalone implementation.

content.value_statement: AI agent projects often lack a clear path from design to validation. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured workflow for agent architecture, tools, memory, orchestration, and evaluation.
actual_capabilities: Breaks AI agent work into design, implementation, orchestration, tools, memory, and evaluation phases.
Recommends related skills for agent architecture, autonomous agents, CrewAI, LangGraph, tools, and evaluation.
Provides copy-paste prompts for each workflow phase.
Defines a simple agent architecture from user input through planning, tools, memory, and response.
Includes quality gates for checking agent logic, tools, memory, orchestration, and evaluation.
limitations: It is a workflow guide, not a complete agent framework or code library.
It assumes referenced companion skills are available in the user environment.
It does not provide production security controls for autonomous tool use.
It requires project-specific testing, permissions, and safety review before deployment.

use_cases.title: Design a New Agent
use_cases.description: Use the phases to define agent purpose, capabilities, tools, memory, and success metrics before implementation.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Multiple Agents
use_cases.description: Plan roles, communication, delegation, and orchestration for a CrewAI or LangGraph based system.

use_cases.title: Review Agent Readiness
use_cases.description: Use the quality gates to check agent logic, tool integration, memory behavior, orchestration, and evaluation coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a single agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this workflow to plan an AI agent for my project. Define the purpose, capabilities, tools, memory needs, and success metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Single Agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Implementation guidance for one autonomous agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this workflow to guide single agent implementation. Help me choose a framework, implement logic, connect tools, configure memory, and test behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multi-Agent Coordination
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for several cooperating agents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this workflow to design a multi-agent system. Define agent roles, communication paths, task delegation, orchestration, and coordination tests.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate an Agent System
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this workflow to evaluate an agent system. Create criteria, test scenarios, edge cases, performance measures, and improvement steps.

output_examples.input: Plan a support triage agent with tool access and memory.
output: A phased plan covering agent purpose, tool interfaces, memory design, and evaluation criteria.
A list of related skills to invoke for architecture, tools, memory, and testing.
Quality gates for validating behavior before deployment.

output_examples.input: Design a multi-agent research workflow using LangGraph.
output: Agent roles for planning, retrieval, synthesis, and review.
A workflow graph outline with state management and conditional branches.
Evaluation scenarios for coordination, failure handling, and final answer quality.

output_examples.input: Review whether my agent project is ready for release.
output: A readiness checklist for logic, tools, memory, orchestration, and evaluation.
Gaps that need more testing or clearer safety boundaries.

best_practices: Start with clear agent purpose, allowed actions, success metrics, and failure boundaries.
Test tools, memory, orchestration, and edge cases before giving agents broader autonomy.
Use the phase prompts in order when scope is unclear, then revisit evaluation after each change.
anti_patterns: Do not connect high-impact tools before defining permissions and rollback plans.
Do not treat the workflow as a substitute for production security, privacy, or reliability review.
Do not skip evaluation when changing prompts, tools, memory, or orchestration logic.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps plan AI agents, multi-agent systems, orchestration workflows, tool integration, memory systems, and evaluation steps.

faq.question: Does it generate complete agent code?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow structure and prompts that guide implementation with other tools or companion skills.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it mention?
faq.answer: It references CrewAI for multi-agent systems and LangGraph for stateful workflow orchestration.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is written as tool-agnostic guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code sessions.

faq.question: Does it include safety controls?
faq.answer: It includes quality gates and scope warnings, but users must add project-specific security and permission controls.

faq.question: Why were security findings reviewed?
faq.answer: The scanner flagged Markdown backticks as possible shell execution. Review found formatting only, with no executable command behavior.
